dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, equipped with the assumption that mu is a probability measure.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: X is measurable with respect to the given measurable structure and the Borel measurable structure on Real.
conclusions: The absolute-exponential infimum scale of the squared function omega -> X(omega)^2 is finite if and only if the quadratic-exponential infimum scale of X is finite.
The absolute-exponential infimum scale of omega -> X(omega)^2 is exactly the square, in ENNReal, of the quadratic-exponential infimum scale of X.
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued Y, define A_mu(Y) as the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero t such that Y is measurable, exp(|Y|/t.toReal) is mu-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
For a real-valued X, define Q_mu(X) as the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero t such that X is measurable, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
Finiteness means strict inequality below the ENNReal top element infinity.
The square Q_mu(X)^2 is ordinary natural-number squaring in ENNReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, every measurable real-valued function X satisfies A_mu(X^2) < infinity if and only if Q_mu(X) < infinity, and in fact A_mu(X^2) = Q_mu(X)^2, where A_mu uses the threshold integral of exp(|Y|/t) and Q_mu uses the threshold integral of exp(X^2/t^2), both bounded by 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem assumes only measurability of X; it does not assume either scale is finite, so the equality also covers the infinite-scale case.
Both scale definitions are ENNReal infima and explicitly exclude candidate scales 0 and infinity before converting a scale to Real.
The result concerns infima, not necessarily attained minima; it does not assert integrability or the bound at the infimum scale itself.
Every candidate admitted to either scale set carries an explicit Integrable condition, avoiding reliance on the totalized integral for nonintegrable functions.
The threshold is exactly 2 in both definitions, with no unspecified multiplicative constants.
The first scale is applied to X^2 and therefore internally uses |X^2|; no separate identity |X^2|=X^2 appears in the proposition.
No centering, independence, symmetry, or moment assumptions beyond measurability are encoded.
ambiguities: The packet gives the complete-order infrastructure for sInf but does not spell out in prose the empty-set convention; under the displayed ENNReal complete-order structure the infimum still has a defined ENNReal value.
The Bochner integral is exposed through an opaque wrapper, but its behavior outside integrability is immaterial inside the admissible sets because Integrable is explicitly conjoined.
The descriptive names A_mu and Q_mu are introduced only for this translation; the dossier itself presents the two constructions anonymously.
